reason: The text explicitly establishes the Israelites as followers of Yahweh through multiple indicators: (1) God identifies Himself as Yahweh (יְהוָה / אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה) to Moses; (2) The Israelites cry out to God (Elohim) from their affliction, demonstrating their appeal to the divine; (3) God reveals His covenant relationship with the Israelites, stating 'I will take you to Me as a people, and I will be your God' (וְלָקַחְתִּ֨י אֶתְכֶ֥ם לִי֙ לְעָ֔ם וְהָיִ֥יתִי לָכֶ֖ם לֵֽאלֹהִ֑ים); (4) God positions the Israelites as a chosen people bound by covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; (5) Moses and Aaron are commissioned as God's representatives to deliver God's commands to the Israelites. These elements establish a follower relationship where the Hebrews are portrayed as Yahweh's chosen people in covenant relationship with Him.
